questions.text: National Emergency under Article 352 can be proclaimed by the President on grounds of ____.

options.text: War, external aggression, or armed rebellion (changed from 'internal disturbance' in 1978)
Financial crisis that threatens the monetary stability of India as a whole
Failure of the constitutional machinery in any particular State of India
Breakdown of public order and law enforcement capacity in a Union Territory

questions.explanation: Article 352 covers three grounds: war, external aggression, and armed rebellion. The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' — a higher threshold requiring active armed revolt, not mere civil unrest. Option B describes Financial Emergency (Art. 360); Option C describes President's Rule (Art. 356).

questions.text: President's Rule (Article 356) is imposed in a State when ____.

options.text: The constitutional machinery of the State has failed or broken down
The State government passes a resolution requesting President's Rule
The Centre faces war and needs to control all State administration
The State Chief Minister loses a floor test in the State Assembly

questions.explanation: Article 356 (President's Rule / State Emergency): imposed when the President, on the Governor's report or otherwise, is satisfied that the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. The Supreme Court (S.R. Bommai case, 1994) ruled that imposition of Art. 356 is subject to judicial review and the Assembly cannot be dissolved before Parliamentary approval.

questions.text: The landmark S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) Supreme Court judgment imposed important restrictions on President's Rule. It held that ____.

options.text: President's Rule proclamation is justiciable; floor test is the only proper test of majority
President's Rule is non-justiciable and solely at Presidential discretion
Governor's report is final and binding; Parliament cannot overturn President's Rule
Only the Supreme Court (not Parliament) can approve or revoke President's Rule

questions.explanation: Bommai (1994): (1) Presidential satisfaction under Art. 356 is justiciable (courts can review it). (2) Floor of the Assembly is the only proper place to test majority — not the Governor's drawing room. (3) State Assembly cannot be dissolved before Parliament approves the proclamation (President can only suspend it). This decisively checked arbitrary imposition of President's Rule.

questions.text: When a National Emergency under Article 352 is in force, which Fundamental Right is expressly suspended by the Constitution itself (not merely restricted)?

options.text: Article 19 rights (6 freedoms) are automatically suspended during war/external aggression
Article 21 (right to life) is suspended automatically upon Emergency proclamation
Articles 14 and 15 (equality rights) are suspended by the President automatically
All Fundamental Rights are equally suspended without any constitutional distinction

questions.explanation: Article 358: During a National Emergency caused by WAR or EXTERNAL AGGRESSION (not armed rebellion), Article 19's six freedoms are AUTOMATICALLY suspended — no separate Presidential order needed. Article 359 allows the President to suspend enforcement of other Fundamental Rights (except Arts. 20 and 21, which cannot be suspended even during Emergency — 44th Amendment guarantee).

questions.text: A proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 must be approved by Parliament within ____.

options.text: One month — by a special majority (2/3 present + majority of total strength)
Six months — by a simple majority in both Houses of Parliament
Two months — by an absolute majority of total Parliamentary strength
Thirty days — by a joint session convened by the President immediately

questions.explanation: 44th Amendment (1978): Art. 352 proclamation must be approved by both Houses within ONE MONTH by a SPECIAL MAJORITY (2/3 of members present and voting + majority of total membership). If approved, it continues for 6 months and can be renewed every 6 months. It can be revoked by the Lok Sabha alone by a simple majority resolution.

questions.text: Article 360 (Financial Emergency) has never been invoked in India. Under what conditions may it be proclaimed?

options.text: When financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened
When the Union government's fiscal deficit exceeds a statutory threshold
When the RBI declares a systemic banking crisis requiring Central control
When foreign exchange reserves fall below a three-month import cover limit

questions.explanation: Article 360: Financial Emergency is proclaimed when the President is satisfied that 'the financial stability or credit of India or of any part thereof is threatened.' During this, the Centre can give financial directions to States, reduce salaries of government employees (including judges), and require States to reserve all Money Bills for Presidential consideration. Never invoked — not even in 1991.

questions.text: India has witnessed three National Emergencies. Which of the following correctly identifies all three?

options.text: 1962 (Sino-Indian War), 1971 (Indo-Pak War / Bangladesh), 1975 (Internal disturbance)
1965 (Indo-Pak War), 1971 (Bangladesh War), 1984 (Operation Blue Star)
1947 (Partition), 1962 (China War), 1971 (Bangladesh Liberation War)
1962 (China War), 1975 (Internal), 1984 (Anti-Sikh riots after assassination)

questions.explanation: India's three National Emergencies: (1) 1962: Sino-Indian War (external aggression); (2) 1971: Indo-Pakistani War / Bangladesh Liberation War (external aggression); (3) 1975–77: proclaimed by Indira Gandhi on grounds of 'internal disturbance' (the Emergency), the most controversial. The 1965 war did NOT lead to a declared Emergency. 1947 and 1984 also did not invoke Art. 352.
